@ a par of an event is computed at the events, and is the array of 0s before the first one
@ a par of an event read in a sum at sample is its last value, 0 before the first event, written inline or in a let
@ a par of an event given to a flow: an event input has the array at each event, a sample input reads the last array
@ a par of an event in an arm is computed at the events even where the arm is not chosen: the frame 6 reads the event of the frame 4, and the frame 0 the default
@ prev~ and delay~ of a par of an event store the array at the event and give the one before it, the one two before it: the arrays of 0s at the first events
@ a part with a block value in the delay of a par is computed at the event with the block value of that time
process 0 params r=10 frames=6 in x=[2 3 4 6 5 8]
process 0 params r=100 frames=6 in x=[10 7 9 12 14 11]
@ vdelay~ of an element of a par of an event is stored at the events, and its length is read at them: d = 1.5 is the mean of the two values before
@ a par in a par is the array of arrays [[m, m + 1], [m + 2, m + 3]]: the outer number i is the row, the inner j the column
@ a par in a par~: each replica k has the part with its own number, and the delay of the replica gives the one before
@ a part with a ^name stored by a delay is the value of the end of the stage: the event of the frame itself, and the delay gives it a frame later
@ a part of an event mixed with x in the first argument of prev~, written inline or in a let, is the part of its replica made at the events: x + m + 2 stored at each frame, 0 before the first event
@ delay~ of 2 of the element 0 stores x + m + 1 at each frame and gives it two frames later
@ vdelay~ of a length 2.0 of x + 2 m + 1 (the replica 1) gives the value of two frames before: the part is 0.0 up to the first event
@ a par~ of delays of a par of an event: the replica k has the part m (k + 1) + 1 of its own, and its own delay
@ a par in a par in the first argument of prev~: the element [1][0] has the part 10 m + 2 (the outer number is the first index, the inner the second)
@ a part with a block value is made at the event with the block value of that time, and a change of the block value between two events does not change it
process 0 params r=10 frames=6 in x=[2 3 4 6 5 8]
process 0 params r=100 frames=6 in x=[10 7 9 12 14 11]
@ the part of a ^name read by a delay written above the maker is the value of the end of the stage: the event of the frame itself, so it is the same as the delay written below the maker

@ a delay written above the maker that saves a part with the name e of an event (not a ^name) saves it where it is written: the event of the frame comes after, so the part is the one of the event before
@ the part e + 2 of a name e saved where it is written is the same inside a par, in a let, in a par~, in a par in a par and in the arms of a match~ as it is outside a par
@ the arms of a match~ with a delay and a par each: every arm stores its x + part at each frame, chosen or not, and the value is the one the chosen arm stored the frame before
@ a par of three in a par of two in the first argument of a delay: the element i = 1, j = 2 stores x + 5 m
